text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.51% today to $141.62, capping a remarkable 13% climb over two weeks as oil prices have surged on Middle East supply concerns. The immediate trigger is escalating geopolitical tensions: Iran threatened U.S. warships, Saudi Aramco facilities were attacked, and the International Energy Agency warned that diesel supply will remain tight into 2027 due to Iran-related disruptions. With global oil trading at $125 per barrel—well above the U.S. benchmark of $96—refiners and oil producers benefit from both higher crude prices and the premium spread between them.

The two-week rally reflects a fundamental shift in market expectations: what looked like mixed signals about Russian diesel supply just yesterday has now been overshadowed by tangible Middle East supply losses and inventory declines. For an integrated energy company like ConocoPhillips, sustained high oil prices and tight refined product markets create a favorable backdrop for both upstream production and any downstream operations.
